summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-10-07 (window Oct 1–7). I found two qualifying candidates, both election-administration blunders in the window, each with two accepted sources opened and quotes checked against the page text. 1) Colorado: about 800,000 ballots in Adams, Arapahoe, Douglas and Weld counties wrongly include the Front Range Passenger Rail tax question (Issue 7A). The rail district apologized for not communicating its new boundaries (CPR and The Gazette, Oct 7). 2) Oxford, Maine: a packaging error at the printer sent out a small number of wrong ballots (Press Herald and WGME, Oct 7). That one is weaker and the same state as the Oct 10 South Portland story, so it's an alternate. Search capacity ran out before I found a third or fourth candidate. Genius: I'm submitting no genius candidates for 2026-10-07. Nothing I found was in the US, inside the Oct 1–7 window, and confirmed by two different accepted publishers. The three science Nobels are all ruled out. Medicine (Deisseroth) and physics (Halzen) have already run on the site. Chemistry (announced Oct 7) went to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai, who are based in France and Japan. Most of the US-led research items I checked were published in journals weeks before the window, and ScienceDaily was simply reposting them late. Several others were led from outside the US or had only one accepted source. The web search tool hit its usage limit partway through the scan. After that I could only open pages already linked from results, so I couldn't look for second sources. No genius story met the standard; nothing published. The verified facepalm story is on the bench for a later day.

candidates.headline: About 800,000 Colorado ballots wrongly include the Front Range Passenger Rail tax question
candidates.reason: passed every check; kept for a later day because the other side had no story

candidates.headline: Packaging error at the printer sends some Oxford, Maine, voters the wrong ballots
candidates.reason: an earlier candidate was published

candidates.headline: New Jersey governor announces more problems found in the MVC voter-registration system
candidates.reason: In the date window (Oct 7; Inquirer and the governor's release). It's an update on a problem first disclosed in July, the governor frames it as a fix of an error from the previous administration, and it touches noncitizen and incarcerated-voter registration. That makes it a contested political story, not a self-evident blunder.

candidates.headline: Calaveras County, Calif., voter pamphlets printed with the wrong candidate statements
candidates.reason: The ABC10 video page still couldn't be fetched. The other coverage (Union Democrat, FOX40, myMotherLode, Calaveras Enterprise, Yahoo) isn't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: State audit finds $160 million error in Iowa DOT financial reporting
candidates.reason: The only coverage found was WHO 13, KCAU and a Yahoo republication, none of them accepted.

candidates.headline: Pender County, N.C., sends incorrect property tax bills
candidates.reason: The only coverage found was Port City Daily and a county release on a press-wire site. Neither is accepted.

candidates.headline: Clerical error leads to ex-MARTA cleaner receiving $620,000 in unearned overtime
candidates.reason: Reported around Sept. 29, 2026, before the 7-day window.

candidates.headline: Champaign County, Ill., suspends early voting after ballot errors
candidates.reason: Coverage is still only on outlets not on the accepted list (WCIA, IPM Newsroom, Fox Illinois, Capitol News Illinois, NPR Illinois, Yahoo), plus a congressional committee release.

candidates.headline: Car theft suspect arrested after asking a North Bay officer for the time
candidates.reason: Reported around Oct. 9–10, 2026, after the scan date. It's also a car theft, which has a victim, and the source (KRON4) isn't accepted.

candidates.headline: 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry awarded to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai for chiral ('mirror') chemistry (Oct. 7)
candidates.reason: Inside the window, but the laureates are based in France and Japan. Not in the US.

candidates.headline: Cornell team finds BC200, a human brain gene that can still jump through DNA
candidates.reason: The ScienceDaily page (Oct. 5) says the Science paper was published Sept. 24, which is before the 7-day window.

candidates.headline: Stanford Medicine drug blocking 15-PGDH regrows knee cartilage in aged mice
candidates.reason: The ScienceDaily page is dated Oct. 6, but the Science paper (DOI 10.1126/science.adx6649) is an earlier publication being reposted. It is also a mouse result.

candidates.headline: University of Illinois physicists find pair density waves persisting above the superconducting transition in uranium ditelluride
candidates.reason: The ScienceDaily page is dated Oct. 7, inside the window. But the PNAS paper page could not be opened, so its publication date is unconfirmed and there is no second accepted publisher.

candidates.headline: NASA JPL-led team measures seasonal movement of Earth's center of mass more precisely
candidates.reason: NASA's own announcement is dated Sept. 16, 2026, which is before the window. The ScienceDaily repost on Oct. 7 is not the event date.

candidates.headline: MIT-led CERN team finds quarks leave wakes in quark-gluon plasma
candidates.reason: The paper is in Physics Letters B with a 2025 DOI, so it is too old. The work was also done at CERN in Switzerland.

candidates.headline: Florida Museum study traces Mississippian-style pottery in Tampa Bay to migrant craftspeople
candidates.reason: Only one accepted source (ScienceDaily, Oct. 6). The American Antiquity publication date was not confirmed, and the journal is not an accepted publisher.

candidates.headline: UCSF brain implant lets people with paralysis speak and gesture at once through an avatar
candidates.reason: The Nature Neuroscience paper was published Sept. 14, which is before the window.

candidates.headline: Harvard/Oregon-led team detects radio waves and a magnetic field from exoplanet Beta Pictoris b
candidates.reason: This is a non-peer-reviewed arXiv preprint posted Sept. 15, before the window. It is also hedged as 'may have' detected.

candidates.headline: Kilauea's repeated lava fountains explained in a USGS-linked Science study
candidates.reason: The Science paper was published Oct. 8, after the scan date.

candidates.headline: Wilmington, Del., historians identify 33 Revolutionary War soldiers buried in an unmarked grave
candidates.reason: The memorial ceremony was Sept. 23, before the window. Smithsonian (Oct. 6) was the only accepted source opened.

candidates.headline: Two new sea spider species described from the Salish Sea
candidates.reason: Led by the University of British Columbia, with dives at Canadian sites, so not in the US. The paper was published Aug. 26.

candidates.headline: 'Phoenix' second-generation planet suspected around white dwarf HS 0209+0832
candidates.reason: Led by the University of Warwick in England; no US lead institution. The result is also framed as a possibility.

candidates.headline: Feathered microraptorine Norellraptor barsboldi shows flight evolved more than once
candidates.reason: The fossil is from China and the team is from China, Italy and Slovakia. Not in the US.

candidates.headline: Optogenetic gene therapy and goggles restore limited sight in 7 of 10 blind patients (NEJM, Oct. 7)
candidates.reason: The research is from Swiss and French groups (IOB Basel, Paris). No US lead institution was confirmed.

candidates.headline: Gut microbe Bacteroides uniformis makes a cholesterol-lowering molecule (Nature, Oct. 7)
candidates.reason: Led by Sun Yat-sen University in China, so not in the US. It is also a mouse study.
